seoH2: A nutrition app that does the counting for you
seoP1: A classic calorie counter asks you to find the food in a list, guess the portion size and type everything in by hand. At three meals a day that is fifteen minutes of admin — and the main reason most food diaries are abandoned in the second week.
seoP2: Plately turns that around. You photograph the plate, and the app recognises the ingredients and breaks the meal down into calories, protein, carbohydrates and fat. One analysis takes about four seconds, and the whole diary is built with a tool you already carry in your pocket.
seoP3: On top of that comes hydration tracking with a goal calculated from your body weight, and a weight chart that shows the trend rather than a single measurement. All of it in one browser tab — on your phone, tablet and computer, with no separate app to install on each device.
useLead: Four situations where keeping a diary starts to pay off.
use1d: You see the deficit as a number instead of guessing at it. The weight chart smooths out daily swings, so you judge the trend rather than one random morning.
use2d: Protein is the macro people miss most often. Plately shows it separately for every meal, so you spot the shortfall the same day instead of a week later.
use3d: Instead of reconstructing a whole week from memory at the appointment, you have the meals, macros and hydration on record. You can export the data at any time.
use4d: If classic trackers have already defeated you, the problem was rarely motivation — it was the number of taps. A photo instead of a form removes that barrier.
faqLead: The short version of how Plately works, what it costs and what happens to your data.
a1: Plately is a nutrition app that runs in your browser. You take a photo of your meal and the app recognises the ingredients and converts them into calories and macros: protein, carbohydrates and fat. Beyond the food diary it also tracks hydration and body weight.
q2: Do I need to install anything?
a2: No. Plately runs in the browser on Android, iOS, Windows, macOS and Linux. Open app.plately.eu, sign in with your Google account, and the same diary is there on your phone and on your computer.
q3: How does counting calories from a photo work?
a3: You photograph the plate, and Plately recognises the ingredients and breaks the meal down into calories, protein, carbohydrates and fat. Analysing a single photo takes about four seconds.
a4: Yes. The Start plan costs 0 USD and needs no payment card and no commitment. It includes 5 meal analyses per day, 3 coach messages per day, and unlimited hydration and weight tracking. None of the plans carry ads.
q5: What do the paid plans cost?
a5: Premium is $6.99 a month or $59 a year: it removes the daily limits on meal analyses and coach conversations, gives 4 AI activity reports a day at any hour, and unlocks a custom accent colour. Ultra is $12.99 a month or $119 a year and raises the reports from 4 to 8. You can change plan in your account settings.
q6: What is the coach in Plately?
a6: It is an assistant that builds its advice from your context: sleep, stress level, activity, diet and any obstacles you report. It refers to what you actually recorded in your diary rather than handing out general rules.
q7: How is the hydration goal calculated?
a7: Your daily goal is derived from your body weight rather than a generic rule such as eight glasses a day. You log what you drink with a single tap: a glass is 250 ml, a bottle 500 ml and a shaker 750 ml.
a8: You sign in with a Google account, and your diary is protected at the database level — nobody but you can read it. Plately carries no ads and no third-party trackers, and you can export or delete your data at any time.
a9: The interface is available in twelve languages: Polish, English, German, Ukrainian, Russian, French, Italian, Spanish, Portuguese, Japanese, Chinese and Korean.
q10: Can I connect my own API key?
a10: Yes. Instead of using the limits of your plan you can connect your own API key in the settings.
q11: Does Plately sync with a watch?
a11: No. Activity figures — steps, heart rate and sleep — are typed in by hand, on every plan. Plately runs in the browser, and the browser has no access to Health Connect, Apple Health or Huawei Health. The plans differ only in how many times a day the AI will write about those figures.
browserReq: Requires a modern browser with JavaScript enabled.
appP1: Plately opens on the day view. The calorie ring shows how much of your daily target you have eaten and how much is left until the evening, and beside it three macronutrient bars — protein, carbohydrates and fat — each with its current value and its limit, so a shortfall is visible immediately. On the right sits the hydration counter, with a goal calculated from your body weight and one-tap buttons for a glass, a bottle and a shaker. Below runs the list of meals logged that day, with calories and macros on every entry.
appP2: The progress tab collects what a single day cannot show: current weight, total lost so far and the distance left to your target. The calorie history chart plots seven or thirty days against the goal line, and the weight chart smooths daily fluctuation, so you read a trend rather than one arbitrary morning. Every measurement is saved with its date and stays in the history.
appP3: The AI coach reads your diary and builds the day's plan out of it: what to eat in the evening to close the protein gap, when to stop adding carbohydrates, how much is still left to drink. You can also simply ask it a question. The last tab is your profile — level, points, day streak, badges and a friends leaderboard. That part usually decides whether a food diary survives longer than two weeks.

howH2: Your first meal in three steps
howLead: From opening the app to the first entry in your diary usually takes less than two minutes.
how1d: Open the app and choose Google sign-in. There is no registration form and no password to invent, and the Start plan asks for no payment card.
how2d: Tap Add meal and take a picture of the plate. Plately recognises the ingredients and, in about four seconds, writes calories, protein, carbohydrates and fat into the diary.
how3d: Fluids go in with one tap and the morning weigh-in with a single entry. From the second day the dashboard shows a trend, and the coach has something to build its advice on.
howNote: The same diary opens later on your phone, tablet and computer — just sign in with the same account.
